h1: The 6 Best Rolling Printer Stands of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Rolling Printer Stands 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six rolling printer stands and carts compared on surface size, locking wheels, drawers, footprint and storage for home offices.
summary: The HUANUO stand is the best all-round rolling printer cart thanks to locking casters and a drawer. The YAOHUOO suits full-size all-in-ones, the GYIIYUO adds real file storage, and the Pipishell is the slimmest cart for tight rooms.
intro: A printer you can roll away is a different appliance from one parked on a desk. It leaves the work surface free, tucks into a closet during video calls, and wheels over to the paper supply when needed. The catch most buyers miss is that wheels without locks turn every paper tray pull into a small slide across the floor.

We reviewed eight rolling carts and stands and kept six that realistically carry a home printer. Rankings come from the spec sheets: top surface size, whether the casters lock, what storage is included, and how much floor space each one takes up.

products.name: HUANUO Printer Stand with Cable Management and Storage Drawer
products.verdict: A purpose-built printer cart with locking wheels, a drawer and tidy cable routing.
products.description:
This HUANUO stand is designed for printers from the start, with a built-in storage drawer, cable management cutouts and locking caster wheels. The maximum shelf height is 14.1 inches, so it slides under a typical desk.

It beats the larger YAOHUOO because the locking wheels and the under-desk sizing solve the two daily annoyances, drift and clutter, in a smaller package at the same low price range. The tradeoff is less top surface, so a bulky all-in-one may overhang.

Choose it for a compact home printer that you want out of sight between jobs. If your machine is a wide office-class all-in-one, step up to the YAOHUOO.
products.idealFor: Compact home printers that live under a desk.
products.skipIf: Your printer is a full-size office all-in-one.

products.name: YAOHUOO 22"x15" Large Printer Stand with Drawer
products.verdict: Real top-surface room for a full-size all-in-one on wheels.
products.description:
The YAOHUOO offers a 22 by 15 inch top surface on a two-tier rolling table with a drawer. That footprint is aimed squarely at full-size all-in-one printers that make smaller stands look cramped.

It ranks second because the bigger top costs floor space and the listing does not highlight wheel locks the way the HUANUO does. In exchange you get a stable platform where scanner lids and trays have room to open.

Best for anyone whose printer outgrew a standard stand. Skip it in a tiny room where every inch of floor counts.

products.name: GYIIYUO 2 Drawer File Cabinet with 24-Inch Extended Desktop
products.verdict: A rolling file cabinet whose extended top doubles as the printer stand.
products.description:
The GYIIYUO combines two letter and A4 drawers with a 24 inch extended desktop on rolling casters. A side storage bag and fabric drawer fronts round out the design.

It ranks below the dedicated stands because the price rises into the next range and it is more cabinet than printer cart. What you gain is genuine filing capacity, so one piece replaces both a stand and a small cabinet.

Ideal for a home office that needs paperwork storage next to the printer. If you only need a place to set the printer, the cheaper stands above are enough.
products.idealFor: Home offices that need files and a printer base together.
products.skipIf: You only need a printer platform.

products.name: DEVAISE 3-Drawer Mobile File Cabinet
products.verdict: Three lateral drawers and a flat top, all on casters.
products.description:
The DEVAISE is a mobile cabinet with three lateral drawers, a rustic brown finish and a flat top suited to a printer. Its caster base lets it roll to where the work is.

It falls below the GYIIYUO because the top is a plain flat surface without the extended desktop, though it gives one more drawer of capacity. The wood-look finish blends into a home office better than a metal cart.

Buy it if storage matters more than printer ergonomics. Skip it if you want an open shelf that keeps paper and cables in easy reach.
products.idealFor: Offices that want hidden filing under the printer.

products.name: Simple Houseware 3-Tier Heavy Duty Metal Utility Rolling Cart
products.verdict: A flexible steel cart that happens to carry a printer well.
products.description:
This is a general-purpose three-shelf utility cart with a heavy duty steel frame and four casters. It is not printer-specific, but open shelves give you a place for the printer, paper and spare ink.

It ranks under the printer stands because it has no drawer or cable management, so cords hang loose. The steel frame is a plus, and it stays in the lowest price range.

Pick it for budget buyers who want a cart that can later move on to the kitchen or craft room. Skip it if you want a tidy, enclosed look.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers wanting a flexible cart.
products.skipIf: You want cable management and a drawer.

products.name: Pipishell 3 Tier Rolling Cart with Wheels and Handle
products.verdict: The narrowest rolling option for a printer in a tight room.
products.description:
The Pipishell is a three-tier open metal cart with a built-in push handle, four wheels and a slim footprint. It slides into gaps beside a desk or fridge that wider carts cannot use.

It ranks last because the narrow shelves suit only compact printers and there is no drawer or cable routing. The handle makes steering easier than on the Simple Houseware, which is the main advantage.

Best for small rooms and compact printers. A large all-in-one will not sit comfortably, so choose the YAOHUOO instead.
products.idealFor: Small rooms with a compact printer.

whatMatters.detail: The top is the platform your printer actually sits on, and if its feet hang over the edge it can tip or rock. Measure your printer's width and depth, then add a couple of inches for the paper tray to open. Check the listing for exact surface dimensions rather than overall cart size.

Casters are the small wheels that let the cart roll, and locking ones hold it still. Without locks the cart creeps every time you pull a tray or press a button. Look for the word locking in the specs, and note how many of the wheels actually lock.

A stand that fits under your desk keeps the printer out of the way. Measure your desk's clearance height and compare it with the listed maximum shelf height. Remember the printer adds its own height on top, so leave a gap.

Drawers hide clutter but make supplies harder to see, while open shelves keep paper in reach but show everything. Think about whether you reach for paper daily. Check what each tier is listed to hold before buying.

A printer needs power and often USB, and loose cords snag on wheels. Cutouts or routing channels keep them tidy and stop the cart from pulling on the outlet when it rolls. Look for cutouts in the title or bullet points.

howToChoose.intro: Printer width decides which stand will work before anything else.

cards.label: Open cart
cards.text: Open carts keep supplies visible and cost less, but cords and clutter show. The Simple Houseware and Pipishell carts are the open options here.

cards.label: Drawer cabinet
cards.text: Cabinets hide files and look tidier, but weigh more and cost more. The GYIIYUO and DEVAISE fit this group, while the HUANUO and YAOHUOO sit between with a single drawer.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to the HUANUO unless they have files to store.

faq.q: Do rolling printer stands work with any printer?
faq.a: Only if the top surface is large enough and the cart is rated for the weight. Measure your printer's footprint first and compare it with the listed top dimensions.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make most often?
faq.a: Skipping the wheel locks. Without them, pulling the paper tray can push the cart away, so look for locking casters on the listing.

faq.q: Is a file cabinet worth it over a basic cart?
faq.a: If you keep paperwork near the printer, yes. The GYIIYUO gives you two drawers and a wide top, saving a separate cabinet.

faq.q: How do I set up the printer on a cart?
faq.a: Place it centered on the top, route the power and USB cords through any cutouts, and lock the casters before you start printing.

faq.q: How do I keep cords from tangling?
faq.a: Use the cutouts on the HUANUO or a cable tie on open carts, and leave enough slack for the cart to roll a short distance.

faq.q: Can I use a utility cart instead?
faq.a: Yes, the Simple Houseware and Pipishell carts work, but they lack drawers and cable routing, so you manage supplies and cords yourself.

finalTake: The HUANUO Printer Stand is the best fit for most home offices, with locking wheels, a drawer and cable cutouts in a compact body. Step up to the YAOHUOO for a big all-in-one, or the GYIIYUO if filing space matters. The open carts are fine when budget or footprint rules everything.
